name: LUM-201
lead: LUM-201 (ibutamoren, formerly MK-0677) is an orally administered growth hormone secretagogue receptor agonist under clinical development for pediatric growth hormone deficiency (PGHD) [2]. It is developed as a daily oral alternative to injected growth hormone.

Phase 2 trials in children with idiopathic PGHD have examined growth responses, and researchers have proposed a pretreatment test to identify children with enough residual hypothalamic-pituitary function to respond [1][6][9]. A Phase 3 placebo-controlled trial is registered and recruiting [4][17]. It is not approved by any regulator.
No published study has tested LUM-201 for appearance outcomes in healthy people.

paras: LUM-201 acts at the GH secretagogue (ghrelin-type) receptor to stimulate pulsatile GH release. In a comparison of 68 children in a PGHD trial, a single dose elicited greater GH responses than standard diagnostic stimuli such as arginine and glucagon [2][10].
A pediatric capsule formulation was reported to show similar pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic responses to the tablet [5].

Phase 2 trials include OraGrowtH210 (n=104, completed), OraGrowtH212 (n=24) and the extension and safety studies OraGrowtH211 and OraGrowtH213 [11][12][14][18]. Researchers reported that the growth response in children with moderate GHD depended on the pattern of GH pulsatility induced by LUM-201, and that a predictive enrichment marker could identify responsive children [1][7][6][3]. Interim analyses reported dose responsiveness in acute GH response, IGF-1 and annualized height velocity [8][9].

A Phase 3 trial against placebo in treatment-naive children is registered and recruiting, with a long-term safety extension planned [4][17][13]. Small Phase 2 studies in fatty liver disease (ibutamoren, n=12) and, planned, with semaglutide in older adults with obesity are also registered [15][16].

timeline.event: Predictive enrichment marker paper and OraGrowtH212 start [1][14].
Phase 3 trial in children registered as recruiting [17].

card.summary: An oral GH-secretagogue (ibutamoren) in trials for children with GH deficiency; nothing tests it for looks.
card.note: Investigational; evidence is in children with diagnosed GHD only.

quick.overview:
LUM-201 is the development name for ibutamoren (MK-0677), a daily oral drug that stimulates the body's own growth hormone release. It is being tested as an alternative to injections in children with growth hormone deficiency.

Phase 2 trials reported growth responses in some children, and a Phase 3 trial is under way. No study has examined it for appearance in healthy people.
quick.mechanism: It activates the GH secretagogue (ghrelin-type) receptor, prompting pulsatile GH release, which in turn raises IGF-1.
quick.risks: It is investigational and not approved. Safety data come from pediatric trials, with long-term safety extensions registered.
